story.setup: When robots look and feel like women, the world has started a countdown to destruction (captions at 0 to 6 s).
story.stakes: Men will have no reason to develop, improve, earn money, or to marry; the state will not forbid it.
story.progression: Claim (no reason for men to develop), the price scenario ('100,000 shekels, like a car'), men will save up, people will say 'I am in love with my robot', the state will not stop it, technology will advance, men will not tell women from robots.
story.payoff: A closing question: she comes Saturday at 16:00 and leaves; would a man buy it?
story.payoff_delivered: partly: the opinion is delivered but ends on an open question

why_it_may_work: Interpretation: a visual spectacle (a humanoid robot) with a clear provocative claim in the first four seconds, frequent cutaways that illustrate each phrase, and a closing question that invites argument; the comment count (731) points to a debate.
why_it_may_underperform: Interpretation: polarising wording and an off-brand tone may repel some audiences; nothing in it leads to Matan's own offer.

standout_moments.what: Cut from the talking head to a walking humanoid robot exactly on 'רובוטים' makes the hook concrete.
Countdown timer cutaway on 'העולם הפעיל סטופר של השמדה' dramatises the claim.
Closing scenario with a specific time, 'שב-16:00', turns the point into a vivid question.
